fairness_facts.evidence: One group-aware split (grouped by claimed sender, test_frac 0.30, val_frac 0.15, seed 7) is computed once per packet-loss level and the SAME idx dict {tr_match, va, te} is passed to run_model for every model, matched and __full alike. Verified empirically: test=26,392 windows / 5,752 positives for every published row, and the reconstructed split reproduces those counts exactly; train/val/test groups are pairwise disjoint.

Matched-N classical models are fitted on exactly Xr[tr_match] where tr_match = matched_train_idx(...) = group-wise cap of the train split at quantum max_train=3000 with seed 7, giving 3,023 windows (whole sender groups are kept, so the cap overshoots 3000 by part of one group). Reconstructed: 3,023 windows, 104 sender groups.

fairness_facts.answer: ALMOST -- run_model re-caps internally to 3000 windows
fairness_facts.evidence: run_model's quantum branch re-applies _cap_train_groupwise to the already-capped tr_match (3,023 > max_train=3,000, so the cap re-runs with the same seed over the SUBSET's groups). Empirically the re-cap returns 3000 of 3,023 windows (23 windows from dropped groups differ).

A single BlockReducer (per-block PCA: 4 mobility + 4 network components, clip [0.5%,99.5%] -> StandardScaler -> PCA -> [0,pi] scaling) is fitted once on the UNCAPPED train split and the same transformed matrix Xr serves the quantum kernels AND the matched classical baselines (quantum: Xr[tr]/Xr[te] at common.py:296-343; classical: Xr[tr]/Xr[te] at 346-354). Verified: Xr has exactly 8 columns.

The __full variants fit on data.X (the 19 raw window features, scaled inside each model's own pipeline) with the train split capped at full_cap=15,000 -> 15,048 windows. The published Table-I '(full N)' rows therefore change BOTH the sample count (3,023 -> 15,048) AND the input representation (8-dim PCA -> 19 raw features) at once; baseline_fairness comparison (ii) disentangles this. The quantum models never see the 19 raw features (the 8 qubits encode the 8 reduced angles).
Matched rows and __full rows are scored on the identical te indices (the same idx['te'] object); every published p=0 row has n_test=26,392, n_pos=5,752.

fairness_facts.answer: Shared but unused by Table-I models
fairness_facts.evidence: va (15% of groups) is carved out identically for all models; the matched classical and quantum SVMs tune by internal CV on the train subset instead (GridSearchCV / group-aware C-grid CV). va is consumed only by the one-class detectors (nu selection) and the LSTM (early model selection), which are not Table-I rows.

fairness_facts.answer: Classical tuned at least as hard as quantum on the SVM axis; quantum has an extra feature-map-training axis, reported openly
fairness_facts.evidence: Classical: GridSearchCV, 5-fold stratified (seed 17), scoring average_precision -- rbf_svm 16 configs/80 fits, random_forest 4/20, mlp 4/20, xgboost 36/180. Quantum: C-grid {0.1,1,10,100} over 5 group-aware folds (20 fits, same AP scoring) PLUS KTA feature-map training (Adam lr 0.05, 200 epochs, batch 512, 1 restart, best-alignment snapshot). qsvm_zz deliberately gets NO map training (fixed-parameter ablation).
